title: BP-0181112b and BP-c552cb0f answer regexes still reject a correct paraphrase (word order, '1.5 seconds')
goal: The answer regex of BP-0181112b matches 'the device object holds the recovery key' as well as the kb's order, and the regex of BP-c552cb0f matches 'a budget of 1.5 seconds'; bench_scenarios.csv and bench_pool.csv change in step and pool check passes

run: import re,sys,json;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import bench_pool as b;R={x['id']:json.loads(x['checks'])[0] for x in b.read_csv(b.PUBLIC_FILE) if x['id'] in ('BP-0181112b','BP-c552cb0f')};r=[bool(re.search(R['BP-0181112b'],'The device object holds the recovery key')),bool(re.search(R['BP-c552cb0f'],'SessionEnd hooks share a budget of 1.5 seconds'))];print(r);sys.exit(0 if all(r) else 1)

gates.question: How do the two answer regexes take the paraphrases: a reverse-order alternative with a bounded in-sentence window, or a looser unordered match (both terms anywhere in the answer)?
options: unordered match of both terms anywhere in the answer

notes: Premise: the repro prints [False, False] and exits 1 on 2026-10-13. BP-0181112b is a scenario row (answer in bench_scenarios.csv, pool row built from it); BP-c552cb0f is an eval row whose regex only bench_pool.csv holds, kept by source on every rebuild, so edit every pool row sharing source lookup_eval.csv:EV-sessionend-hook-input-fields-reason-budget. A new regex still matches a line of the question's pack (pool check says so). Planned at the 2026-10-13 draft triage (sprint 5 of 15, "Benchmark pool rows: answer regexes, stale rows, the gap row, a pool build that asks before paying and a corrected report"): it serves the fitness tests of EP-gzr4mmkm: a lookup's verdict or the benchmark's measurement is wrong until it is fixed.
